name: Warrior on a Horse (Statue of Alexander the Great)
description: A massive bronze statue in the main square of Skopje, widely regarded as representing Alexander the Great. It is one of the city's most iconic landmarks.

name: Kozjak Lake
description: Kozjak Lake is the largest artificial lake in North Macedonia, surrounded by scenic mountains and cliffs, popular for hiking and photography.

name: Matka Canyon
description: A stunning canyon near Skopje, home to monasteries, caves, and one of the world's deepest underwater caves. Popular for kayaking, hiking, and boat rides.

name: Ohrid Lake
description: One of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes, a UNESCO World Heritage site, shared between Macedonia and Albania. Known for crystal-clear waters and cultural heritage.

name: Church of St. John at Kaneo
description: A 13th-century Macedonian Orthodox church overlooking Lake Ohrid, famous for its cliffside location and Byzantine architecture.

name: Kokino Megalithic Observatory
description: A Bronze Age archaeological site and ancient observatory, ranked among the oldest observatories in the world. Known as 'the Macedonian Stonehenge'.

name: Millennium Cross
description: A 66-meter high cross situated on the top of Mount Vodno, overlooking Skopje. Built to commemorate 2000 years of Christianity.

name: Pelister National Park
description: The oldest national park in North Macedonia, located on Baba Mountain. Famous for its Molika pine forests and two glacial lakes known as 'Pelister's Eyes'.

name: Heraclea Lyncestis
description: An ancient city founded by Philip II of Macedon in the 4th century BC. Known for well-preserved Roman mosaics and ruins.

name: Mavrovo Lake
description: A man-made lake within Mavrovo National Park, surrounded by mountains and popular for skiing, fishing, and the submerged church of St. Nicholas.
